title: Maps out of a localised module are the maps out of the module, when the target has invertible actions

standard_prerequisites.name: Description of a localised module by fractions
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets an element of the localisation be written as m/s, which is what both injectivity and surjectivity are checked on.

standard_prerequisites.name: Invertibility of the actions of the elements of S on N
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The hypothesis of the statement, used at lines 1401 and 1409
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the action of s to be undone when defining the extension and when showing the map is determined by its values on M.

core_obligations: Injectivity: for a map out of the localisation and an arbitrary fraction m/s, use s alpha(m/s) = alpha(m/1) to express alpha(m/s) as the inverse action of s applied to alpha(m/1), so the map is determined on the image of M (proof lines 1400-1403).

Surjectivity: given a map beta on M, define the extension by sending a pair (m, s) to the inverse action of s applied to beta(m), check it respects the equivalence relation and is well defined (proof lines 1404-1412).
Verify R-linearity of the extension by an explicit computation with two fractions and common denominators (proof lines 1413-1427).
proof_roadmap: Show a map out of the localisation is determined on M (proof lines 1398-1403).
Build the extension by inverting the action and check linearity (proof lines 1404-1428).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a multiplicative subset S and R-modules M, N on which every element of S acts invertibly, the canonical map from Hom of the localisation into N to Hom of M into N is an isomorphism (statement lines 1387-1396). The proof does not cite the adjunction between localisation and the modules with invertible actions: it shows injectivity by computing that a map on the localisation is determined by its values on M, builds the extension on pairs and checks well-definedness against the equivalence relation, and verifies linearity by a common-denominator computation (proof lines 1398-1428). The explicit well-definedness and linearity checks are the substance, and the author writes them all out. H2.
